title: If statements
examples: What happens if I use two if statements?
Can I check more than one condition at once?
What is the difference between if and else if?

explain.say: Today we learn about making decisions in code.
A condition is a question that must be true or false.
We use comparison operators to test these conditions.
The else statement runs only if the first condition is false.
If we have many checks, we use else if to keep testing.

items: Path 3: True -> Run ELSE IF code
Path 4: False -> Run final ELSE code

draw.text: If... Else If: Testing many options

explain.say: In real life, checking if it is raining tells you what to do.

faq.q: What happens if I forget the else statement?
faq.a: The code will run, but it will not have a path for when your first condition is false. You might miss important instructions.
asks: What if the condition is false?
Do I need an else block always?

faq.q: Can I use 'and' to check two things at once?
faq.a: Yes, you can combine conditions using 'and'. Both parts must be true for the code to run. For example, age must be greater than ten and score must be above eighty.
asks: How do I check multiple things?

faq.q: What is the difference between == and =?
faq.a: The equals sign, two equal signs, checks if something is equal. The single equals sign is used to give a value to a variable. They do very different things in coding.
asks: Which equals sign do I use for checking?

faq.q: Does the code stop after the first true condition?
faq.a: Yes, in an if-else if chain, the code stops running as soon as it finds one true condition. It will skip checking the rest.
asks: Does it keep checking after one success?

faq.a: A boolean value is simply a true or false answer. This is the basic type of data that conditions test.
asks: What kind of answer is a condition?
Is true and false the only answers?

facts: A condition evaluates to either true or false.
Comparison operators include greater than, less than, and equals.
The else statement provides a default action.
If-else if structures test conditions sequentially.

quiz.say: If score is greater than 80, print A. Else if score is greater than 50, print B. Otherwise, print C. If the score is 75, what will the code print?
quiz.show: If score > 80: A. Else if score > 50: B. Else: C. Score 75?
quiz.why: The code checks if 75 is greater than 80, which is false. Then it checks if 75 is greater than 50, which is true, so it prints B and stops.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the code only runs the block for the first true condition it finds.
wrong.2: This is wrong because 75 is not greater than 80, so the first condition fails.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the code stops at the first true condition, which is the second one.

quiz.say: Which operator checks if two values are exactly the same?
quiz.why: The double equals sign, ==, is the standard way to check for equality in programming logic.

wrong.0: A single equals sign is used to assign a value, not to check if two things are equal.
wrong.1: This checks if one number is greater than or equal to the other, which is a comparison, not an equality check.
wrong.2: This checks if one number is less than or equal to the other, which is a different type of comparison.

quiz.say: If a program checks if a user's age is 18, and then checks if their citizenship is 'Citizen', which structure is best if both must be true?
quiz.why: When two conditions must both be true for the code to proceed, you combine them using the 'and' logical operator.

wrong.0: Separate if statements will run the code block for each true condition, which might run twice.
wrong.1: Using 'or' means only one condition needs to be true, not both.
wrong.2: While possible, using 'and' is cleaner and more direct for checking simultaneous requirements.
